description: A four-bit binary up/down counter that can be preset to a number and that carries in and out for chaining.

inputs.text: A rising edge advances the count by one, up or down according to the UP/DOWN input.
While this is high the count is held at 0 and every Q output is at 0V.
Sets the direction: high counts up, low counts down. Unpatched it counts as low, so the counter runs backwards.
One bit of the number the counter is loaded with while PRESET EN. is high: P1 is worth one, P2 two, P3 four and P4 eight.
While this is high the count is forced to the number on the P inputs and the clock is ignored.
While this is high the clock is blocked and the count is held; patch the carry output of another CD4516 here to chain the two.

outputs.text: The least significant bit of the count, worth one.
The second bit of the count, worth two.
The third bit of the count, worth four.
The most significant bit of the count, worth eight.
0V at the end of the count — 15 going up, 0 going down — and 10V the rest of the time, so it goes low for one count in sixteen.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
The counter advances on the rising edge of the clock, despite the maker's tooltip on that jack reading "Negative edge triggered".
